lit: as if there were no such matter

use.how: Mostly adverbial (若无其事地走开) or after 装作/表现得. Describes a person acting calm and normal after something that should affect them.

near.diff: 满不在乎 is genuinely not caring at all; 若无其事 is outward calm, often hiding what one feels or what one has done.

cue: Your roommate broke your favourite mug, dropped the pieces in the bin and sat down to dinner chatting normally. How did they act?

ctx.s: 他打碎了杯子，怕被妈妈发现，就{若无其事}地继续看电视。
ctx.en: He broke the cup and, afraid Mum would find out, carried on watching TV as if nothing had happened.

ctx.s: 被老板批评后，她眼圈都红了，却还是{若无其事}地回到座位上工作。
ctx.en: After being told off by the boss her eyes were red, yet she went back to her desk and worked as if nothing had happened.

ctx.s: 你们昨天吵得那么凶，你今天怎么还能{若无其事}地跟他打招呼？
ctx.en: You two had such a big fight yesterday. How can you say hello to him today as if nothing happened?

ctx.s: “别担心，见到他我会装作{若无其事}的样子。”
ctx.en: "Don't worry, when I see him I'll act as if nothing has happened."

ctx.s: 明明心里很难过，她却表现得{若无其事}，还笑着安慰大家。
ctx.en: She was clearly hurting inside, yet she acted as if nothing was wrong and even smiled and comforted everyone.

ctx.s: 小偷把钱包塞进口袋，然后{若无其事}地走出了商店。
ctx.en: The thief slipped the wallet into his pocket and strolled out of the shop as if nothing had happened.

bad.s: 这里很安全，{若无其事}，你放心吧。
bad.en: (meant: it's safe here, nothing will happen, don't worry)
bad.why: It describes a person's calm manner after something happened, not a place or situation where nothing happens.

bad.s: 听说自己中了大奖，他激动得{若无其事}。
bad.en: (meant: hearing he had won the big prize, he was beside himself with excitement)
bad.why: It means looking calm and unaffected, so it cannot describe someone overcome with excitement.

mean: both just as bad as each other; six of one, half a dozen of the other
lit: half a jin and eight liang: in the old system a jin had sixteen liang, so both weigh the same

use.how: Predicate after two people or things compared: 你们俩半斤八两。 Says neither is better, usually that both are equally poor.

near.diff: 不相上下 is a neutral or admiring 'evenly matched'; 半斤八两 implies both are equally bad and is mocking.

cue: Two brothers each blame the other for their messy room, but both are equally untidy. What do you tell them about each other?

ctx.s: 你们俩的字都写得不好看，{半斤八两}。
ctx.en: Neither of you has nice handwriting; you're as bad as each other.

ctx.s: 别笑他了，你的英语跟他{半斤八两}。
ctx.en: Stop laughing at him; your English is no better than his.

ctx.s: 这两家餐厅服务都很差，{半斤八两}，去哪家都一样。
ctx.en: Both restaurants have terrible service; there's nothing to choose between them, so either one will do.

ctx.s: “你说哥哥懒？你们俩{半斤八两}！”妈妈说。
ctx.en: "You say your brother is lazy? You're just as bad as each other!" said Mum.

ctx.s: 两个候选人都没什么经验，说起来是{半斤八两}。
ctx.en: Neither candidate has much experience; really, it's six of one and half a dozen of the other.

ctx.s: 这场比赛踢得太难看了，两个队谁也别笑谁，{半斤八两}。
ctx.en: It was an awful match; neither team can laugh at the other, they were as bad as each other.

bad.s: 两位钢琴家都弹得非常精彩，真是{半斤八两}。
bad.en: (meant: both pianists were brilliant and evenly matched)
bad.why: It mocks two parties as equally bad; it cannot praise two people as equally excellent.

bad.s: 这件衣服{半斤八两}，不贵也不便宜。
bad.en: (meant: this garment is so-so, average)
bad.why: It compares two parties with each other; it does not describe one thing as mediocre.

lit: to have no home one can return to

use.how: Attributive (无家可归的人) or predicate, often after 让/使: 大火让很多人无家可归。 Said of people or animals with no home at all.

cue: After the flood washed their houses away, the villagers had no roof over their heads and nowhere to go. What had they become?

ctx.s: 冬天到了，城里有一些{无家可归}的人需要帮助。
ctx.en: Winter has come, and there are homeless people in the city who need help.

ctx.s: 这家收容所专门照顾{无家可归}的猫和狗。
ctx.en: This shelter specialises in looking after homeless cats and dogs.

ctx.s: 志愿者每周给{无家可归}的老人送饭。
ctx.en: Volunteers bring meals every week to elderly people who have no home.

ctx.s: 他被房东赶了出去，一时{无家可归}，只好住在朋友家。
ctx.en: His landlord threw him out, and with nowhere to live for the moment he had to stay at a friend's.

ctx.s: 这场大火让几十户人家{无家可归}。
ctx.en: The fire left dozens of families homeless.

ctx.s: 小说讲的是一个{无家可归}的孩子在大城市里长大的故事。
ctx.en: The novel tells the story of a homeless child growing up in a big city.

bad.s: 我今天加班，{无家可归}，晚上很晚才回去。
bad.en: (meant: I'm working late and won't get home until late)
bad.why: It means having no home at all, not being away from home for a while.

bad.s: 家人都在南方，他一个人在北京，很{无家可归}。
bad.en: (meant: he is homesick and lonely)
bad.why: It means literally having no home, not a feeling of missing home, and cannot be graded with 'very'.

use.how: Usually a complement: 消失得/跑得/逃得无影无踪, or a predicate. Said of people, things or feelings that disappear completely.

near.diff: 一干二净 is doing something completely (forgot, ate, cleaned); 无影无踪 is something vanishing from sight with no trace left.
烟消云散 is mostly worries, anger or doubts melting away; 无影无踪 is mainly people or things vanishing from sight.

cue: You put your phone on the café table, turned to order, and when you looked back it was simply gone, not a sign of it anywhere. What happened to it?

ctx.s: 我一转身，小猫就跑得{无影无踪}了。
ctx.en: The moment I turned around, the kitten had run off and vanished.

ctx.s: 太阳一出来，雾就消失得{无影无踪}。
ctx.en: As soon as the sun came out, the fog disappeared without a trace.

ctx.s: 刚才还在桌上的钥匙，怎么一下子就{无影无踪}了？
ctx.en: The keys were on the table just now; how have they vanished just like that?

ctx.s: 他借了钱以后就{无影无踪}，电话也打不通。
ctx.en: After borrowing the money he vanished without a trace, and his phone can't be reached.

ctx.s: 那艘小船越漂越远，最后在海面上消失得{无影无踪}。
ctx.en: The little boat drifted further and further away until it vanished without a trace on the sea.

ctx.s: 警察赶到时，那个骗子早已逃得{无影无踪}。
ctx.en: By the time the police arrived, the con man had long since disappeared without a trace.

bad.s: 这个房间{无影无踪}，什么家具都没有。
bad.en: (meant: this room is empty, there's no furniture)
bad.why: It says something has disappeared; it does not describe a place as empty.

bad.s: 他是个{无影无踪}的人，很少说话。
bad.en: (meant: he is a quiet, low-profile person)
bad.why: It is not a personality trait; it describes a disappearance.

mean: quietly, without a word to anyone

use.how: Mostly adverbial: 不声不响地走了/做完了. Said of a person doing something quietly without telling or disturbing anyone.

near.diff: 不辞而别 is only leaving without saying goodbye; 不声不响 is doing anything quietly without announcing it.

cue: Your colleague never mentioned it, then one day you learn she had quietly finished a master's degree at night. How did she do it?

ctx.s: 他{不声不响}地走进教室，坐在最后一排。
ctx.en: He slipped quietly into the classroom and sat in the back row.

ctx.s: 吃完饭，她{不声不响}地把大家的碗都洗了。
ctx.en: After the meal, she quietly washed everyone's bowls without a word.

ctx.s: 你怎么{不声不响}就辞职了？连我都不知道。
ctx.en: How could you just quit without telling anyone? Even I didn't know.

ctx.s: 平时{不声不响}的小李，这次竟然拿了全公司第一名。
ctx.en: Xiao Li, who usually keeps so quiet, actually came first in the whole company this time.

ctx.s: 这家小店{不声不响}地开了二十年，回头客特别多。
ctx.en: This little shop has quietly been open for twenty years and has lots of regulars.

ctx.s: 他{不声不响}地准备了一个生日惊喜，让女朋友感动得哭了。
ctx.en: He quietly prepared a birthday surprise that moved his girlfriend to tears.

bad.s: 图书馆里很{不声不响}，大家都在看书。
bad.en: (meant: the library is quiet, everyone is reading)
bad.why: It describes a person acting without a word to anyone, not a place being quiet.

bad.s: 听到这个噩耗，她{不声不响}地大哭起来。
bad.en: (meant: hearing the terrible news, she burst out sobbing)
bad.why: Loud sobbing contradicts it; it means making no sound and saying nothing.

mean: ungrateful, not knowing what is good for one
lit: not to know good from bad

use.how: Predicate, often 真不知好歹 or 别不知好歹. Reproaches someone who rejects or resents kindness or good advice.

near.diff: 恩将仇报 is actively harming a benefactor; 不知好歹 is failing to appreciate kindness, refusing or resenting it.

cue: You stayed up late helping a friend fix his CV, and all he did was complain that you changed too much. What do you call him?

ctx.s: 我好心提醒你，你还生我的气，真是{不知好歹}！
ctx.en: I warned you out of kindness and you're angry with me? You really don't know what's good for you!

ctx.s: 别{不知好歹}了，老师批评你是为你好。
ctx.en: Don't be so ungrateful; the teacher criticised you for your own good.

ctx.s: “我请你吃饭，你还挑三拣四，怎么这么{不知好歹}？”
ctx.en: "I'm treating you to dinner and you're still picky? How can you be so ungrateful?"

ctx.s: 妈妈给他找了份好工作，他却嫌累不去，亲戚们都说他{不知好歹}。
ctx.en: His mother found him a good job, but he wouldn't go because it was tiring, and the relatives all said he didn't know what was good for him.

ctx.s: 他扶起摔倒的醉汉，那人却骂他多管闲事，真{不知好歹}。
ctx.en: He helped up a drunk who had fallen, and the man swore at him for meddling. How ungrateful.

ctx.s: 故事里，老仆人好心劝告少爷，那个{不知好歹}的少爷却把他骂了一顿。
ctx.en: In the story, the old servant gave the young master well-meant advice, and the ungrateful young master just gave him a scolding.

bad.s: 这孩子还小，{不知好歹}，分不清哪种蘑菇有毒。
bad.en: (meant: the child is too young to tell which mushrooms are poisonous)
bad.why: It reproaches someone for rejecting kindness, not an innocent inability to tell things apart.

bad.s: 这道题太难了，我{不知好歹}，不会做。
bad.en: (meant: this question is too hard, I don't know the answer)
bad.why: It is not about lacking knowledge; it is a reproach for ingratitude.

lit: not up to one's own control

use.how: Adverbial before a verb: 不由自主地笑了/往后退. Says a movement or reaction happened on its own, before the person decided anything.

near.diff: 情不自禁 is a feeling welling up (joy, tears); 不由自主 covers any involuntary action, including bodily reflexes.
身不由己 is being forced by circumstances or others; 不由自主 is an automatic, unwilled reaction.

cue: The bus braked hard and, before you could think, your whole body lurched forward. How did you move?

ctx.s: 一紧张，我就{不由自主}地咬指甲。
ctx.en: Whenever I get nervous, I bite my nails without meaning to.

ctx.s: 车突然刹住，大家都{不由自主}地往前一冲。
ctx.en: The bus braked suddenly and everyone lurched forward involuntarily.

ctx.s: 看到那条大狗，他{不由自主}地往后退了一步。
ctx.en: When he saw the big dog, he stepped back without thinking.

ctx.s: 冷风一吹，他{不由自主}地打了个哆嗦。
ctx.en: When the cold wind blew, he shivered involuntarily.

ctx.s: 听到有人叫自己的名字，他{不由自主}地回过头去。
ctx.en: Hearing someone call his name, he turned his head without thinking.

ctx.s: 他说话的时候，总是{不由自主}地摸鼻子。
ctx.en: When he talks, he always touches his nose without realising it.

bad.s: 我{不由自主}地报名参加了这个比赛。
bad.en: (meant: I signed up for the contest on my own initiative)
bad.why: It means involuntary, not 'by my own choice'; a deliberate decision is the opposite.

bad.s: 他的工作很{不由自主}，老板说什么他就做什么。
bad.en: (meant: he has no freedom at work, he does whatever the boss says)
bad.why: It describes a reflex action, not a lack of freedom at work, and cannot be graded with 'very'.

use.how: Usually a predicate after the thing counted: 游客不计其数。 Also 多得不计其数. Says a number is far too large to count.

near.diff: 成千上万 gives a scale, thousands upon thousands, and sits before a noun; 不计其数 says the number is beyond counting and usually follows it.

cue: Asked how many fan letters the old singer received over his career, his manager just laughed: nobody could ever have counted them. How many?

ctx.s: 夏天的夜空里，星星{不计其数}。
ctx.en: In the summer night sky there are countless stars.

ctx.s: 这些年他帮助过的学生{不计其数}。
ctx.en: Over the years he has helped more students than anyone could count.

ctx.s: 春节期间，回家的旅客{不计其数}。
ctx.en: During the Spring Festival, countless travellers head home.

ctx.s: 网上关于减肥的文章{不计其数}，可真正有用的没几篇。
ctx.en: There are countless articles online about losing weight, but hardly any are actually useful.

ctx.s: 这家博物馆收藏的古书多得{不计其数}。
ctx.en: This museum holds more old books than can be counted.

ctx.s: 他说过的谎话{不计其数}，谁还会相信他？
ctx.en: He has told countless lies. Who would believe him now?

bad.s: 我们班的学生{不计其数}，一共三十个。
bad.en: (meant: our class has lots of students, thirty in all)
bad.why: Thirty is easily counted; it is only for numbers too large to count.

bad.s: 他{不计其数}地喜欢这本书。
bad.en: (meant: he likes this book enormously)
bad.why: It describes how many things there are; it is not an intensifier for feelings.

lit: not going beyond what was predicted

use.how: Usually at the start of a clause (不出所料，他又迟到了) or after 果然. Says something that has happened matched a prediction.

near.diff: 出乎意料 is the opposite: the outcome was a surprise.

cue: Everyone guessed the lazy team member would miss the deadline, and on Friday he did exactly that. How do you begin telling the story?

ctx.s: {不出所料}，他又迟到了。
ctx.en: Just as expected, he was late again.

ctx.s: 天气预报说今天有雨，{不出所料}，下午就下起了大雨。
ctx.en: The forecast said rain, and sure enough, it poured in the afternoon.

ctx.s: 他平时从不复习，这次考试{不出所料}没及格。
ctx.en: He never revises, so predictably he failed the exam this time.

ctx.s: “我就知道他会答应，果然{不出所料}！”
ctx.en: "I knew he would say yes, and that's exactly what happened!"

ctx.s: 比赛结果{不出所料}，冠军还是去年那支队。
ctx.en: The result was as expected: the champions were the same team as last year.

ctx.s: 公司宣布涨工资后，{不出所料}，辞职的人少了很多。
ctx.en: After the company announced a pay rise, as everyone expected, far fewer people quit.

bad.s: 我没想到他会来，真是{不出所料}！
bad.en: (meant: I never thought he would come, what a surprise!)
bad.why: It means things went exactly as predicted, so it cannot express surprise.

bad.s: 明天考什么还{不出所料}，我心里没底。
bad.en: (meant: tomorrow's exam is unpredictable, I'm not sure)
bad.why: It confirms an outcome that has already happened as predicted; it does not mean unpredictable.

mean: to talk on and on in a flood of words
lit: surging like a flood that never stops

use.how: Predicate or adverbial: 他滔滔不绝地讲着. Said of a fluent, unbroken stream of talk, neutral or admiring.

near.diff: 喋喋不休 is annoying, petty chatter and always critical; 滔滔不绝 is a fluent stream of words, often neutral or admiring.

cue: Ask your uncle one question about his fishing trip and he talks for forty minutes without pausing for breath. How does he talk?

ctx.s: 一说到足球，他就{滔滔不绝}。
ctx.en: Once he starts on football, he talks on and on.

ctx.s: 两个老同学见了面，{滔滔不绝}地聊到半夜。
ctx.en: When the two old classmates met, they talked nonstop until midnight.

ctx.s: 你平时说话{滔滔不绝}，怎么面试时一句话都说不出来？
ctx.en: You normally talk a mile a minute. How come you couldn't get a word out in the interview?

ctx.s: 会上他{滔滔不绝}地讲了一个小时，各种数据张口就来。
ctx.en: At the meeting he spoke fluently for an hour, reeling off figures without a pause.

ctx.s: 记者只问了一个问题，他就{滔滔不绝}地回答了十几分钟。
ctx.en: The reporter asked just one question, and he answered in a flood of words for over ten minutes.

ctx.s: 老教授{滔滔不绝}地讲着古城的历史，学生们听得入了迷。
ctx.en: The old professor spoke at length about the ancient city's history, and the students listened spellbound.

bad.s: 我病了一个星期，咳嗽{滔滔不绝}。
bad.en: (meant: I've been ill for a week and can't stop coughing)
bad.why: It is only used for a flood of spoken words, not for coughing or other noises.

bad.s: 他{滔滔不绝}地说了一句“谢谢”。
bad.en: (meant: he said 'thank you')
bad.why: A single short phrase contradicts it; it describes a long, unbroken stream of talk.
